analysis:
The supplied units are base lines 1780-2293 (the ensureModelLoaded load path) and head lines 1-587 (file header, config, actor state, setModels). The patch excerpt shows the real change is the KV re-slice helper. It adds a `minimumGrantBytes` parameter to `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` and a new static `minimumGrantBytes(_:)` helper. It is applied in resliceKeepsSlotsServiceable, the reserve-preflight path near head 1043, and the reslice-and-build path near head 1210. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the head text units do not reach the changed ranges, so I could not inspect the changed code directly. The excerpt shows a pure refactor in the standalone local server. It threads per-slot serviceability floors into grant computation so a re-slice does not shrink a resident slot below its minimum KV grant. No new inputs, network surface, key handling, attestation, or cache-storage behavior appears in what I saw.

The viewable code gives no sign of regression against T-041 or TB-007. The cache/weight-hash plumbing (modelArtifactSHA256, cacheEligibleWeightHash, the bracketed pre/post-load hash decision) appears in the unchanged base text and is not shown as changed. `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` traps on duplicate model IDs. That behavior pre-existed in the inline form; the excerpt shows it was only moved into the helper. Slots are keyed by model ID, so I see no new duplicate-key trigger.

Open question for integration: confirm that the `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` signature change (default value or call-site updates) and the changed bodies at head ~1215-1237 and ~1381-1393 keep the serviceability-floor refusal and the unwind and regrow ordering intact. Those regions are not visible in the units provided.
